newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Trucks sees continued European price pressure.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Trucks sees continued European price pressure.

text.p: Volvo Trucks, a unit of Swedish automotive group AB Volvo, said on Thursday it expected continued price pressure in Europe, particularly on the British and German markets.
"We have noted a relatively stronger price fall in Britain and Germany where Mercedes is increasing its activities," Volvo Trucks president Karl-Erling Trogen said at a company seminar.
"The European market is profitable and we have increased the rate of manufacturing," he said.
Trogen said he expected the total European market to amount to close to 170,000 trucks in 1997 and he said European order intake was strong.
Volvo Trucks is meeting competition by cutting costs.
"For example, we only discuss price cuts, not price hikes, with our suppliers," Trogen said.
In North America, Volvo Trucks' order intake rate has increased by more than 10 percent so far this year compared to the same period last year but operations are still posting a loss, Trogen said.
"We are still making a loss in North America but we see a continued and stable improvement," Trogen said, adding that the introduction of the VN model is going well.
In South America Volvo Trucks has increased production by 50 percent so far in 1997 following the strong market growth and it expects to take market share, Trogen said.
Outside core markets, Iran and the former Soviet republics are growing the most and Volvo Trucks talks with the Chinese authorities about establishing the company in China are on track, Trogen said.
